title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Photoirradiation that generates ligand or framework radicals can couple optical switching to static and dynamic magnetism in Yb(III) and Dy(III) molecule-based magnets.
explanation: In a Yb(III) 2D coordination polymer, UV converts 9-anthracenecarboxylate to a radical, adding a spin center, raising susceptibility, and increasing the SMM barrier. Dy-SMM nodes in 2D MOFs undergo photoinduced electron transfer; the resulting radicals change the crystal field and shorten inter-ligand distances, combining room-temperature photochromism with a magneto-optical response. Viologen units in lanthanide tetrahedral cages separately give light-driven host–guest charge transfer and dark catalytic decomposition.
scope: Photoactive lanthanide coordination polymers, 2D Dy-SMM MOFs, and viologen-containing lanthanide cages.
conditions: UV or other photoirradiation sufficient to generate radicals or charge-transfer states.
caveats: Magnetic-barrier gains are not quantified in the review, and the cage example is catalytic rather than an SMM.
